name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+23 district lean makes this one of the most Republican seats in the country
Crawford holds a roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage over Green
Incumbent Crawford is running again with no polls or expert ratings flagging competitiveness
Prediction markets price Republican win odds near 97%
model.rationale: The district's R+23 lean, Crawford's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial edge leave Green without a visible path; with no polls or raters signaling competitiveness and markets near 97% Republican, the safe Republican rating stands.
model.watch: A dramatic national wave toward Democrats or an unforeseen scandal involving Crawford could tighten the race, though nothing currently points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arkansas's First District is among the most Republican-leaning House seats in the country, and Rick Crawford has held it since 2011. He enters the general election with about $1 million on hand after raising roughly $944,000, while Democrat Terri Green has raised about $65,000 and reported under $13,000 in the bank. Libertarian Steve Parsons is also on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings target the race, and prediction markets put Republican odds near 97%.

With no polling available, the forecast rests on the district's heavy Republican lean, Crawford's incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. The expected margin is roughly 19 to 20 points Republican, with wide uncertainty typical of unpolled races. Barring an extraordinary shift in the national environment, the seat appears safely in Republican hands.
